_meta.record_kind_why: This file is written and revised by a person, entry by entry, and no program produces it. It therefore names no producer script and carries no producer hash, and the two freshness gates of this tree reported it for months as an artifact of unknown origin. That count was answering the wrong question about it: there is no run to have made this file, so 'which code wrote it' has no answer rather than a missing one. The declared kind is read by checks/chk_artifact_provenance.py, which owns the vocabulary of kinds and decides what each one means; this file only states which kind it is.
_meta.what_is_still_asked_of_it: Everything that is about the contents rather than the origin. Each entry is still bound to a PAIR of hashes and dies the moment either stops matching, and the gates still refuse to treat a certificate as an exemption for a file. Declaring the kind removes one question that cannot be put to this file, and removes no check on what it says.

_declaration.what_this_is: A neutrality certificate. Each entry states that a producer's bytes moved from one hash to another and that the move CANNOT have changed any figure in the named artifact. The freshness gate may treat such a pair as reconciled instead of stale, and must report it under its own heading rather than folding it into fresh.
_declaration.why_it_exists: An artifact records the sha256 of its producer, so any edit makes a correct artifact stale and only a run restores the match. That is right when the edit could have moved a number and is pure bookkeeping when it could not. On 2026-07-31 a batch of eleven nodes was rerun after a consolidation and returned ZERO moved leaves across 15 168, confirming what the equivalence bench had predicted in seconds. Paying a node's full runtime to make a hash match, when the numbers are proven fixed, buys accounting and not correctness.
_declaration.what_makes_an_entry_admissible: Two things, and neither is an opinion. The bench in scripts/equiv lifts the OLD spelling verbatim out of git by anchor and runs it against the replacement over 4284 cases spanning 21 input classes, four budgets and three magnitudes, including draws placed exactly on the site's declared tolerance and one unit in the last place either side. And the alpha-renaming comparator, built on the tree's own edit-stripping code, shows the remaining difference to be renaming alone. An entry names which of the two carries it.
_declaration.when_an_entry_dies: The moment either hash stops matching. If the producer is edited again, the pair no longer describes reality and the artifact is stale until a new proof or a run. A certificate is never a permanent exemption for a file, only for one pair of bytes.
_declaration.what_it_never_covers: A producer whose edit could move a figure, a node that walks the raw tape (its input is deleted after parsing, so nothing about it can be shown unchanged), and any artifact that gained a NEW field, because a field that does not exist yet cannot be proven equal to itself.
_declaration.how_a_span_is_composed: Added 2026-08-01. An entry is keyed on the pair (recorded, on disk), so a producer edited twice is owed a statement about the whole distance between those two hashes and not about its last leg. Where the recorded blob is still in git the whole distance is compared in one step and the entry carries one proof. Where an earlier leg is not a renaming -- a consolidation that moved a computation into a shared module is not -- the entry states TWO proofs and the point at which they meet, because a distance covered by two number-preserving edits is number-preserving and a distance covered by one proof and one assumption is not. Each such entry names the hash where the legs join, so a reader can check the join rather than take it.
_declaration.evidence: scripts/equiv (parent repository), run 2026-07-31: 17 sites, 4284 cases, zero disagreements on any null carrying numbers. The renaming comparator is calibrated, as of 2026-08-02, on thirteen fixtures cut from one live file of this tree, seven owed a pass and six owed a refusal, thirteen correct; and on a second pass of six further fixtures over three residues, three owed a firing and three owed silence, six correct. The bench is scripts/equiv/bench_c_rename.py and it exits non-zero on any calibration failure.
_declaration.what_was_corrected_2026-08-02: The paragraph that stood here from 2026-08-01 described this rebuild as done. It was not. What was on disk until 2026-08-02 was the earlier set of TEN fixtures with ONE failure among them, and the bench discarded what its own report function returned, so it printed that failure and left the shell with status zero. A caller reading the status read a pass. Both defects are repaired, and the repair is the reason the count above may now be taken at face value. The underlying fault was in the fixtures and not in the comparator: three of the ten renamed EARLY_DAYS and LATE_DAYS, which commit cf780a0 had already renamed to EARLY_DAYS_OVERRIDE and LATE_DAYS_OVERRIDE, so those three transforms substituted nothing and scored the comparator on two identical files. Two of the three were POSITIVE cases and passed while testing nothing; the third was a NEGATIVE case and therefore read as a comparator failure that belonged to the fixture. Every fixture now raises if its transform leaves its input unchanged, and the two constants it renames are read out of the file rather than spelled into the bench, so the next rename in the tree breaks the fixture loudly. Three cases the earlier set never tested were added and all three are load-bearing for the entries below: a reworded function docstring, a reworded MODULE docstring, and an added comment.
_declaration.what_the_second_pass_adds: Added 2026-08-02. The skeleton this comparator stands on removes pure output statements whole, which is right for its own question and leaves two blind spots that were being caught by hand instead. A rename finished everywhere except inside a printed format string leaves the old spelling in the text a reader quotes, and the skeleton, having dropped that statement, calls the pair a renaming. A rename left half-finished inside such a statement leaves a name that nothing binds, which is a file that raises rather than one that computes. The second pass asks three questions the skeleton discarded the evidence for: which names the new version reads and nothing binds, which names the old version bound and the new one does not while a string still spells them, and whether what the file prints is identical once names are normalised and text is kept. None of the three overturns the neutrality verdict, because none of them is a claim about a number; each is reported beside it.
_declaration.what_the_2026-08-11_move_added: A THIRD ROUTE, and it is declared here rather than smuggled in under one of the two above. On 2026-08-11 the tree stopped being a heap: 137 files moved into directories by group. A moved script must be told where the shared modules are, so its bytes change, and 43 artifacts went stale against producers whose edit is a change of ADDRESS. Neither of the two routes above answers that question -- the numeric bench compares columns and the alpha comparator asks about renaming -- so a third is named: the path-edit comparator, described in each entry that uses it, with its calibration. An entry now names which of the THREE carries it. The route rests on two things measured per entry: the whole recorded-to-disk distance reduces to path expressions and imports, and every input the run declared is still on disk with its recorded sha256 intact, so the file the run read is the same file under a new name. Where the second of those cannot be measured the entry is refused, and eight were.
_declaration.what_the_move_did_to_the_entries_that_st: All fifteen died, and by this file's own rule rather than by a decision. An entry is keyed on the artifact's path and on a pair of hashes; the artifacts moved into group directories, so not one of the fifteen keys matches a file today, and most of the hash pairs had already been overtaken by real reruns. They are kept below under superseded_by_the_2026-08-11_move because several of them carry reasoning that is still true and is written nowhere else -- which renames were checked against the whole tree, which strings were left alone because they reach an artifact -- but they are out of `certified`, where the gate reads, because a dead entry left among the live ones inflates the count of what stands on a proof.
_declaration.what_the_2026-08-13_run_form_edit_added: A FOURTH ROUTE, and like the third it is declared here rather than smuggled in under one of the others. Two passes over the same headers on 2026-08-13, both to the instruction a reader is told to follow and neither touching a statement: 101 lines gave up a run form that ignores the pinned versions, and 22 lines gave up a script address the 2026-08-11 move had emptied. Over the whole distance all 41 edited files parse to the same tree. None of the first three routes answers that -- the numeric bench compares columns, the alpha comparator asks about renaming, the path-edit comparator asks about addresses -- so a fourth is named, the documentation-only comparator, and it is the narrowest of the four: it does not argue that a changed computation gives the same answer, it argues that no computation changed. 23 of the 41 files are named as a producer by 34 artifacts. One is a run journal set aside by its own declared kind and three were RUN rather than certified, so 30 entries are owed and 30 stand below: 13 fresh before this edit and carried by one leg, 17 already resting on a 2026-08-11 path-edit certificate and therefore carried by two legs that name their join. WHAT THIS EDIT ALSO DID, AND NO CERTIFICATE HERE COVERS IT: the same files are declared as INPUTS by other artifacts, and checks/chk_input_freshness.py asks about inputs and has no certificate mechanism at all. After the four runs it reports six artifacts outside its declared debt, of which ONE stands on an input edited here and five stand on artifacts of other work in flight. That debt is real, it is reported by that gate in its own words, and it is named here so that a reader does not take a green freshness column for the whole account.
_declaration.what_the_run_form_edit_did_to_the_entrie: Seventeen died, by this file's own rule rather than by a decision: an entry is keyed on a PAIR of hashes, and the producer moved again. Each of the seventeen is replaced above by a two-leg entry that carries its reasoning forward word for word and names the hash where the old leg ends and the new one begins, so nothing established on 2026-08-11 has to be taken on trust or established twice. The dead entries are kept below rather than deleted, and out of `certified`, where the gate reads, because a dead entry left among the live ones inflates the count of what stands on a proof.
_declaration.what_a_real_run_does_to_an_entry_here: An entry is owed only while no run has been paid for. On 2026-08-13 four nodes were run because the same edit had moved them out of freshness on the INPUT side as well, and that question has no certificate mechanism at all. A node that has actually run needs no proof about its producer's bytes, so its entry is moved here rather than left in `certified`, where it would inflate the count of what stands on a proof rather than on a run. The entries are kept rather than deleted because each names the distance it covered and the run does not.
_declaration.what_the_2026-08-20_documentation_edit_a: No new route. A pass removed process commentary from comments and docstrings across the tree: sentences that described how the writing of this code was organised, or pointed at tooling that is not part of this repository, rather than describing what the program does. Where a boundary was real -- one directory, not published in this repository, held a separate strand of work and was out of scope for several gates -- it was stated as a path and referred to CONTRIBUTORS.md. Most producers touched were rerun, because their runtime is seconds and a run is worth more than a proof. TWO were not, and they are the two entries added to `certified` today: mm_bakeoff.py at 1296.6 s and maker_econ.py at 2041.6 s. WHAT THAT PASS ALSO DID TO THIS FILE, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH READING: eleven entries in `certified` no longer described any pair of bytes. THREE died today, one because its producer was edited and two because their node was actually rerun. The other EIGHT were already dead at HEAD before that day, and no instrument had said so, because the freshness gate asks whether a live mismatch is excused and never asks whether an excuse still matches anything. They are moved into their own section rather than deleted, by the rule this file states about itself: a dead entry left among the live ones inflates the count of what stands on a proof. The count that matters is therefore not 50 but what remains in `certified` after this move.
